change: The Unix super-user query uses rustix::process::getuid().is_root() instead of a direct unsafe libc call. The public result remains Ok(real UID == 0); Windows behavior and the separate account-name lookup are unchanged.
source_evidence: Pinned rustix 1.1.5 process/id.rs delegates getuid to backend/ugid/syscalls.rs. The selected libc backend makes one libc::getuid call, converts its unsigned ID to Uid, and is_root compares it with Uid::ROOT (zero). Uid construction debug-asserts that the OS did not return the invalid all-ones UID; no retry or effective-ID substitution is introduced.
dependency: Enabled process on existing rustix 1.1.5 with std/fs/use-libc unchanged. No Cargo.lock package version changes. cargo deny --all-features check and cargo audit passed. Established dependency unsafe is separate trust, not first-party elimination within the dependency.
fixture: Before replacement, the independent /usr/bin/id -r -u fixture passed on Linux. After replacement, it and the existing no-error fixture passed. The test changes no credentials, environment or current directory.
inventory: Expected process/native.rs source blocks 7 to 6; Linux and macOS compiler primary spans 8 to 6. Windows unchanged. Full gate and native verification pending.
deletion: The direct getuid call in is_super_user is deleted; no parallel super-user implementation remains. Integrate within the current migration milestone.
validation: Focused Linux tests and dependency checks passed. Independent review, cargo xtask pr and native validation pending.
exclusions: No fixture changes process credentials or constructs differing real and effective UIDs; the distinction is supported by pinned wrapper source
The integration fixture requires the native id utility on supported Linux/macOS runners
No Miri claim for the native identity call
